posts.name: Swati Jain
posts.cooked:
cat /etc/passwd | tr ':' ',' | head -n 30 | tail -n 10 | sort -k4,4 | cut -d, -f3 | head -n 1

  • cat /etc/passwd | → using cat command to pipe output of /etc/passwd
  • tr ':' ',' → Trims or replaces occurence of : with , (comma)
    eg - syslog:x:102:106::/home/syslog:/usr/sbin/nologin turns into syslog,x,102,106,/home/syslog,/usr/sbin/nologin
  • head -n 30 → gets first 30 lines
  • tail -n 10 → gets last 10 lines from the head -n 30
  • sort → sorts the lines
  • -k4,4 (-kstart, end) → start - 4th column, end - 4th column, i.e., sorts the 4th column in ascending order
  • cut -d, -f3 → cuts the 3rd column based on , as delimiter gets the 3rd field
    eg - syslog,x,102,106,/home/syslog,/usr/sbin/nologin becomes → 102 (3rd column)
  • head -n 1 → prints the topmost line, since sorted in ascending order so lowest number.

So it takes the lines, replaces : with , gets the first 30 lines then last 10 lines from that and sorts based on 4th field in (lexicographical order - 10 will come before 2 reason being 1<2), then cuts on 3rd field and prints the lowest number based on the above sorting.

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
No, the answer given is correct, there is slight mistake in the explanation above.

sort -k4,4 means sort by 4^{th} column, and only that. But how does sort know what a column is? By default spaces are used to determine column, however as you can see here, the columns are , separated. You have to specify that to sort using -t , otherwise, it will use spaces for column splitting. As such, here the sort is thus sorting alphabetically by the entire line (so the first column, as its all unique). Hence _apt row comes on top, and answer is actually 104.

I will encourage students to actually run the commands to verify, instead of speculating, as this is a practical course, and there is always a single truth.

Screenshot 2025-10-23 at 21.01.001646×1056 264 KB

Also note, there is a small mistake in the question,

here we should not have the tr ':' ',' part, as you can clearly see output still has : in it.

posts.cooked:
Thanks for correcting me. @sayan

@Jeet_D I apologize for the misunderstanding.
